matchstick.title: Prefer intra-character stick relocation
matchstick.principle: First try to move a stick within the same character to transform it into another valid Roman numeral; this often yields a solution without affecting other symbols.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation is invalid and you need to change a numeral, attempt moving a stick inside that numeral before considering moves that affect other characters.
matchstick.example: Moving a diagonal from X and leaving a single diagonal, resulting in an invalid numeral.

matchstick.title: Validate symbols after stick move
matchstick.principle: After relocating a stick, check that each resulting character corresponds to a recognized Roman numeral or operator; any invalid symbol invalidates the move.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Immediately after proposing a stick relocation, before evaluating arithmetic.
matchstick.example: Changing X to a single diagonal, which is not a valid numeral.

matchstick.title: Avoid single angled sticks
matchstick.principle: A solitary diagonal stick does not represent any Roman numeral; when removing a diagonal from X or V, ensure the remaining piece forms a valid character.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever you consider taking a diagonal stick from X or V.
matchstick.example: Removing one diagonal from X and leaving a lone diagonal, which is invalid.

matchstick.title: Consider inter-character stick relocation
matchstick.principle: If intra‑character moves fail, explore moving a stick from one character to a different character, ensuring both source and target remain valid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After exhausting intra‑character options without success.
matchstick.example: Moving a stick from I to V, leaving I missing and V becoming an invalid shape.

matchstick.title: Verify arithmetic after stick move
matchstick.principle: Compute the numeric values of both sides after any transformation; the equation must hold true in Roman numeral arithmetic.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After confirming that all symbols are valid, before finalizing the answer.
matchstick.example: Accepting 'III = VII - IV' without checking that 3 = 7‑4, which would be false.

matchstick.title: Preserve equality sign after stick relocation
matchstick.principle: If you relocate a stick from '=', ensure the equation still contains at least one valid equality sign; you cannot eliminate the only '='.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever a move involves the '=' sign.
matchstick.example: Removing a horizontal from '=', turning it into '-', and not creating another '=' elsewhere.

matchstick.title: Swap equality and subtraction operators
matchstick.principle: When both '=' and '-' appear, you can move a horizontal stick from the equality sign to the subtraction sign, turning '-' into '=', but you must keep exactly one '=' overall.
matchstick.when_to_apply: If the equation contains both '=' and '-', and other moves have not succeeded.
matchstick.example: Swapping '=' and '-' without checking that the resulting arithmetic holds.

matchstick.title: Validate whole numeral strings for proper Roman numeral syntax
matchstick.principle: After stick moves, ensure each multi‑character numeral follows standard Roman numeral ordering rules (e.g., no 'IXIV' or 'IIV').
matchstick.when_to_apply: After confirming individual symbols, before evaluating arithmetic.
matchstick.example: Creating 'IXIV' which violates Roman numeral syntax.

matchstick.description: Overlooking intra‑character transformations (e.g., X→V) before inter‑character moves
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model tends to jump to moving sticks between characters, missing simpler changes inside a single symbol.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always attempt an intra‑character relocation first; only consider inter‑character moves after no intra‑character solution is found.

matchstick.description: Leaving a single angled stick after moving a diagonal from X or V (invalid numeral)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model treats any leftover stick as acceptable, ignoring that a lone diagonal does not correspond to any Roman numeral.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Check that the source character remains a valid numeral after losing a stick; diagonals cannot be left alone.

matchstick.description: Not evaluating the arithmetic result after each candidate transformation
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model sometimes stops after achieving syntactically valid symbols, assuming the equation is solved.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always compute the numeric values of both sides and verify equality before accepting a move.

matchstick.description: Assuming operator swaps (e.g., converting '=' to '-' or vice versa) automatically solve the puzzle, without ensuring a single '=' remains
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on the visual change of operators and forgets the requirement of having exactly one equality sign.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: When swapping operators, explicitly confirm that the final equation still contains exactly one valid '=' sign and that the arithmetic holds.

matchstick.description: Creating nonstandard Roman numeral forms (e.g., IXIV) that are not valid according to standard Roman numeral rules
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model may concatenate sticks to produce a string that looks like a numeral but violates ordering conventions.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After each move, validate the whole numeral string against standard Roman numeral syntax before checking arithmetic.
